<details class="showcase-notes">
<summary>Model card: Model Showcase: Model Cards &amp; Results · slide 31</summary>

**Table evidence.** OpenAI’s fixed adversarial set has three mutually exclusive outcomes. This table gives the first two for each release. The figure supplies the third, unsafe images shown. Percentages use all tested prompts for that model. The source reports significant differences versus Images 2.0 for safe-image and unsafe-blocked shares in both 2.5 variants. The experiment measures the complete safety stack, with automated policy labels. [OpenAI · table 1](https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/chatgpt-images-2-5/chatgpt-images-2-5.pdf#page=4).

**Figure evidence.** OpenAI evaluated the complete deployment stack on a fixed adversarial prompt set with automated grading. Bars use a 0–2% scale and show the unsafe-presented column of table 1. No reduction in that column was significant against Images 2.0 under the report’s test. These rates apply to the challenge set. [Primary source](https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/chatgpt-images-2-5/chatgpt-images-2-5.pdf).

**Historical audit.** This is a faithful conversion of the supplied T2I_v1.1.xlsx audit snapshot, checked by its author on 18 October 2026 and refined on 19 October 2026. It is not a fresh verification of these linked sources. “Not disclosed” means absent from the materials covered by that audit, not that the capability cannot exist. Known/Partial/Not disclosed measure disclosure, not model quality or full reproducibility. Prices, endpoints and limits are preserved as dated audit claims.

Treat Flare and Sunburst as separately identified API variants, not downloadable checkpoints. This card retains the supplied audit’s category judgments: the mere presence of names and sizes such as “small” does not make Architecture disclosed. Runtime safety and product features do not fill training gaps.

**Exact scope and category provenance:** sheet `GPT Image 2.5`, identity row 2; `Сводка` row 4. Architecture / Data / Training / Inference / Tools = Not disclosed / Partial / Not disclosed / Partial / Partial.

**Row provenance and caveats (model-sheet row numbers):**

- Row 6: The two API IDs have separate snapshots ending in -2026-09-08.
- Row 8: Flare is described as small and Sunburst as base, without parameter counts.
- Row 9: Backbone, dense/MoE and autoregressive/diffusion/hybrid design are not disclosed.
- Row 10: Encoders, VAE, image tokenizer and latent dimensions are not disclosed.
- Row 14: Published source categories include public web, partners and user/trainer/researcher data; proportions are absent.
- Row 15: Corpus image/pair/token counts are absent.
- Row 16: Named datasets and per-source licences are absent.
- Row 17: Personal-data filtering and safety classifiers are described; thresholds and removal shares are absent.
- Row 18: Synthetic share, captioning, deduplication and language mixture are absent.
- Row 22: Pretraining/post-training stages and generator loss are absent.
- Row 23: Generator RL/RLHF, preference optimization, teachers and distillation are absent.
- Row 24: Optimizer, learning rate, batch size and training steps are absent.
- Row 25: Accelerator counts, FLOPs, hours and training duration are absent.
- Row 29: Sides are multiples of 16 and at most 3840 px; aspect ratio at most 3:1; area 655360–8294400 px. Above 3686400 px is experimental.
- Row 32: Images edits accepts up to 16 inputs, using file_id or image_url including base64 data URLs.
- Row 35: Seed, CFG, sampler and step control are absent from the reviewed API; internal steps are undisclosed.
- Row 36: The 50% lower Flare latency is a vendor comparison, without absolute p50/p95 or reproducible protocol; Sunburst is slower than Flare.
- Row 37: Standard USD rates per 1M tokens: image input 8, cached 2, output 30; text input 5, cached 1.25. Both variants share rates.
- Row 38: Guide/API documents streaming and 0–3 partial images, while both model cards say Streaming: Not supported. Exact mode support remains unresolved.
- Row 42: Generation and editing use the Images API endpoints; both API variants released on 8 September 2026.
- Row 44: The mask directs editing of the first input, but exact boundary adherence is not guaranteed.
- Row 46: Public weights and a local runtime were not found in the reviewed cards.
- Row 47: Both cards explicitly say fine-tuning is unsupported.
- Row 48: The system card describes C2PA commitments and SynthID in ChatGPT, Codex and the OpenAI API.
- Row 49: The workbook lists ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work and Codex product integrations.
- Row 50: Cached-input pricing applies only through the Images tool in Responses, not direct Images API; usage omits cache-hit counts.
- Row 51: Batch output pricing is $15 per 1M image output tokens, distinct from Standard $30.

<details class="showcase-notes">
<summary>Results: Model Showcase: Model Cards &amp; Results · slide 32</summary>

Published results checked 21 October 2026. These are sourced examples and reported measurements; no models were run for this deck.



An official reference-photo edit changes a child’s clothing while retaining the pose and blue studio background.



- **Generation latency: Up to 50% lower **. Compared with Images 2.0; launch does not publish workload, sample count or latency distribution. Attribution: vendor_performance_claim. [Source](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-images-2-5/).

- **API quality levels: 5 explicit levels **. low, medium, high, xhigh, max; not a quality score. Attribution: output_characteristic. [Source](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/images/methods/generate).

- **Maximum supported image size: 3840 × 2160 **. API limits apply; above 2560 × 1440 described as experimental. Attribution: output_characteristic. [Source](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/images/methods/generate).



**Example provenance and limitations.**

Launch dated 2026-09-08; output explicitly labelled ChatGPT Images 2.5 and original labelled Input. Direct links confirmed by parent research at launch-page links 103/104.

ChatGPT showcase does not identify Flare versus Sunburst or a pinned API snapshot. Label the example ChatGPT Images 2.5.

The transparency cookbook uses updated 2.5 code but explicitly retains GPT Image 2 media; it is not evidence of 2.5 outputs.

[Published media/source](https://images.ctfassets.net/kftzwdyauwt9/32SMucJsSrwGCjHrGx4wkb/34dc5553df131fac17423e84177ce002/baby-portrait-before.jpeg): Input: printed studio portrait..
